## wrkq.campaign.canonical-portfolio-authority

- **scope:** campaign lifecycle, exclusive membership, labels, and producer-owned portfolio projections
- **predicate:** A wrkq campaign container is the canonical portfolio resource. Its independent lifecycle is draft, active, completed, or cancelled; container kind and archive state are not lifecycle fields. Draft campaigns may have resident or explicitly enrolled tasks. Effective membership is exclusive resident-or-enrolled, and the task campaign field is the only explicit enrollment authority. Terminal campaigns retain existing members and permit departure but reject every new resident or enrolled admission path, including create, move, copy, and task update. Campaign labels are the existing task-label value type exactly: ordered string arrays preserve whitespace, case, duplicates, and order; an empty array clears and the projection is never null. Campaigns have no canonical owner, schedule, or priority fields. Generic wrkq.container.update remains restricted to slug/title. wrkq.container.campaignPortfolio is the producer-owned collapsed portfolio read model. It returns the complete selected set in one read transaction, without pagination or member identities; omitted filters select unarchived draft+active campaigns, ordered by createdAt descending then UUID ascending. Counts and top-level project footprint derive from current effective members. lastActivityAt is exactly max(campaign.updated_at, effective-member.updated_at). wrkq.container.timelineView is the lazy member detail projection and returns member project identity, footprint, labels, and the same activity definition. Downstream Epic/portfolio displays are consumer views, not mutation or dual-write authorities.

## wrkq.collaboration-ledger.authority

- **scope:** durable agent-collaboration rooms, envelopes, obligations, attendance, and their HRC/ACP consumer boundary
- **predicate:** wrkq is the sole durable authority for collaboration state that must survive every agent runtime: work-keyed rooms, single-addressee envelopes, fan-out groups, reply obligations, membership, attendance, and presentation receipts. Task addressing coalesces strictly to the task's effective campaign when one exists; campaign-adorned and project-kind containers resolve to their respective rooms, while other container kinds are not room authorities. Every mutation preserves wrkq.attribution.caller-principal-exact and human participants use the existing scope-less agent:<id> principal grammar. Rooms have no collaboration lifecycle that can gate traffic. A say into a known, resolvable room is never refused because its work is terminal, its activity is stale, or it carries the hidden discovery label; obligations in every such room enter the same kicker and stop-hook reads. Work and activity are read-time projections only. last_activity is the maximum of room opened, envelope created, and member joined timestamps, and activity is the first matching value: stale for terminal work older than four hours, active when younger than twenty-four hours, and quiet otherwise. The hidden label affects default listing only. HRC owns execution state and actuation only: sessions, generations, runtimes, runs, presentation formatting, kicker drive attempts, stop-hook enforcement, and summon/placement. HRC consumes the wrkq ledger and may write its runtime identifiers only as opaque presented_to join data; it holds no second durable collaboration copy. wrkq never imports HRC, and wrkc must persist, read, and monitor collaboration with every HRC daemon unavailable. A bodyless HRC pending-reply intent for one completed drive attempt is execution actuation, not a second collaboration copy. For a successful drive that presented exactly one envelope, or one fan-out group from one sender, HRC may derive the reply from its canonical dispatcher turn-response projection and emit it through the existing ordinary say surface with exact seat-principal attribution, deterministic auto-reply:<driveAttemptId> idempotency, and auto: turn_final provenance. wrkq remains authoritative for both envelope discharge and whether that say committed. After every uncertain write outcome, HRC establishes commitment only by reading the authoritative envelope row bearing that exact sender and idempotency key; the HRC intent never stores the reply body or decides room, envelope, or obligation state. The non-atomic discharge-read/plain-say race is limited to and accepted by wrkq.collaboration-ledger.auto-reply-manual-race. ACP may persist a rebuildable mobile presentation projection of immutable envelope identity, content, addressing, and creation time, fenced by the wrkq ledger incarnation. That projection is not collaboration authority, excludes mutable obligation, envelope-state, attendance, and presentation-receipt state, and is retired rather than combined across a wrkq ledger replacement. Cross-node collaboration travels through the shared canonical wrkqd ledger. After the fleet-complete cutover, HRC federation retains birth, placement, and summon authority but no durable message transport or message outbox authority.
- **enforced_by:** `T-07612 rev 2 ratified boundary, its rev 3 amendment revision 2, the approved T-07789 auto-reply amendment, and the amended ledger/routing and consumer/cutover evidence bundles`

## wrkq.handoff.caller-owned-scope

- **scope:** agent/project scope + principal resolution for handoff mutations crossing the wrkq RPC boundary
- **predicate:** Handoff scope is CALLER-owned but NOT project-root. The production CLI caller layer in internal/rpccli resolves the effective agent/project scope via internal/scope.Resolve from --scope OR agent-runtime env (--scope -> AGENT_SCOPE_REF -> ASP_SCOPE_REF -> ASP_HANDLE -> ASP_AGENT_ID+ASP_PROJECT), and for CREATE it enforces self-scope (scope.EnforceSelfScope: refuse writing a handoff that targets another agent) BEFORE submitting. The handoff RPC methods (wrkq.handoff.create / get / listView / acknowledge) receive ONLY the EXPLICIT effective fields — scopeRef / agentId / projectId for create+list, actorAgentId / principalRef / acting scopeRef for create+acknowledge. They MUST NOT read AGENT_SCOPE_REF, ASP_SCOPE_REF, ASP_HANDLE, ASP_AGENT_ID, or ASP_PROJECT: scope resolution + self-scope enforcement are caller semantics, not a server read-model concern. The server owns ONLY the durable semantics it can prove without authenticated identity: the handoff.created / handoff.acknowledged events, the idempotency replay + payload-mismatch conflict, the acknowledge etag CAS, the "already acknowledged" mapping, the not-found contract, and explicit-param CONSISTENCY. Explicit-param consistency (protocol integrity, NOT authenticated self-scope): for CREATE the explicit scope tuple is coherent IFF `scopeRef == "agent:"+trim(agentId)+":project:"+trim(projectId)` when scopeRef is present. A supplied scopeRef must be EXACTLY that canonical project ref — fail fast, do NOT silently normalize. Task/role-qualified refs, agent-only refs, unparsable refs, and mismatched agent/project refs are ALL WRKQ_VALIDATION before any write, event, or dry-run projection. An empty scopeRef synthesizes the canonical project ref from agentId/projectId. The server proves this from the params alone (no env, no auth); accepting a same-agent/project TASK ref would otherwise persist with scope_kind=project so canonical project listView misses the handoff while a task-scoped listView sees it — corrupting scope filtering, idempotency scope, and event-payload interpretation. RISK (LOW, accepted): server-side self-scope is UNENFORCEABLE without an authenticated transport, so caller-side enforcement + explicit params is the correct factoring for workrpc. A future authenticated wrkqd MAY add server-side validation WITHOUT changing the DTO field shape.
- **enforced_by:** `internal/scope.Resolve + scope.EnforceSelfScope at the caller call sites + explicit effective-scope params on the handoff methods (the server never reads ASP_* env); daedalus ruling hrcchat#10211 (T-05117)`

- **scope:** human confirmation + interactivity for destructive mutations crossing the wrkq RPC boundary
- **predicate:** RPC mutation methods are NON-INTERACTIVE and deterministic: they accept caller-scoped selectors + EXPLICIT intent (mode, target fields, principalRef) + machine-checkable preconditions (ifMatch, expected impact), and they decide purely from those params. The CLI mirror (internal/rpccli) owns ALL human interaction — the legacy prompt text, abort, --yes, dry-run, and non-TTY rendering — AND the project-root scoping, BEFORE it builds RPC params. ## wrkq.project-root.caller-semantics

- **scope:** project-root path/selector scoping across CLI surfaces
- **predicate:** All path/selector-taking production CLI commands in internal/rpccli must transform raw user arguments through the neutral internal/projectroot implementation BEFORE constructing RPC params or store lookups: raw args + config.Load project-root precedence (WRKQ_PROJECT_ROOT / ASP_PROJECT / .env.local / config.yaml) + --project override (resolved against the DB) + per-command defaultToRoot + ID/UUID/sequence/`t:`/`c:`-prefix exemptions -> effective selector/path RPC methods receive ONLY effective selectors/paths. They must NOT inspect WRKQ_PROJECT_ROOT, ASP_PROJECT, or --project — project-root scoping is caller semantics, not a server read-model concern. There is exactly ONE implementation of this transform; rpccli may wrap it but must not fork it. CONTAINER-SELECTOR ABSOLUTE FALLBACK (T-07701). A container selector naming a campaign may resolve to a container in ANOTHER project, so the caller layer MAY apply a narrow fallback: resolve the SCOPED form first, and only when that does not resolve, re-resolve the RAW selector as an absolute path. The fallback is a fallback, never an exemption — scoped-first is mandatory, a selector that resolves under the caller's own root always wins, and the error surfaced for a genuinely missing path still names the SCOPED path. It applies only to a multi-segment selector whose first segment names a top-level container of kind `project`, so a bare slug is never silently re-pointed at another project's container. It lives in the one rpccli scoper wrapper (`containerSelectorWithAbsoluteFallback`), not in internal/projectroot, and never in an RPC method: the server still receives one already-resolved selector and still reads no project-root env or flag.
- **enforced_by:** `internal/projectroot (single source of truth) + rpccli scoper call sites`
- **source:** `internal/projectroot/projectroot.go`, `internal/rpccli/scope.go`

## wrkq.rpc.remote-transport-locator

- **scope:** wrkq/wrkf CLI database locator, shared remote workrpc transport, and transport-derived logical-node identity
- **predicate:** Day-to-day `wrkq` and `wrkf` commands select their durability endpoint through a database locator, not always a filesystem path. `WRKQ_DB` and the production `wrkq --db` flag MAY accept either a local SQLite path or a remote wrkq semantic RPC endpoint (`rpc://host[:port]`, default port owned by wrkqd). `WRKQ_DB_PATH`, `WRKQ_DB_PATH_FILE`, `wrkqadm --db`, `wrkqd --db`, and `wrkq server --db-path` remain local-path-only inputs and must reject endpoint URLs before any call to `db.Open`. A remote endpoint is a transport to the SAME workrpc method catalog and DTO/error contract exposed by `wrkq rpc --stdio`; it is not the legacy wrkqd REST surface, not a sync peer, and not a second semantic API. Remote clients must complete transport authentication plus `rpc.initialize` before business calls and verify protocol version, protocol schema hash, and required method/capability surface. Migration readiness is server-owned: a production workrpc entrypoint must refuse exposure while any migration embedded in its running binary is pending. A successful authenticated `rpc.initialize` may rely on that server-side readiness gate. `database.migrationHash` is diagnostic identity only; remote clients must not compare migration filenames or infer compatibility from that hash. Network/auth/ handshake failures are transport errors and must not be reported as SQLite contention such as `WRKQ_DB_BUSY`. When remote calls require logical-node provenance, wrkqd derives nodeId only from a bearer token mapped server-side to one valid, non-reserved federation nodeId; caller-supplied node labels and peer IP are never identity. Each token maps to exactly one node, while one node MAY hold several distinct tokens so rotation does not require an authentication gap. Missing and unknown tokens are authentication refusals, and a token repeated anywhere in the mapping is a configuration error. Once a per-node mapping is configured it supersedes the legacy shared token; the shared-token compatibility mode exists only while per-node identity is disabled and cannot supply node provenance to methods that require it. The authenticated nodeId must remain attached to the server-side request context so node-attributed writes such as `claimed_node` can derive it without accepting request data. The node-token set is configured explicitly through `--node-tokens` or `--node-tokens-file` (and their WRKQD env equivalents), never inferred from topology. Bearer values must not appear in errors, logs, or a detached server's process arguments; the file form is the production secret-management surface. In remote mode the canonical host owns the SQLite database, migrations, etags/CAS, attribution writes, event log, search/index sidecar and embedder, attachment store, and monitor/watch bounded read models. The caller host owns project-root argument scoping, prompts, stdin/stdout, local file reads/writes, presentation, and polling loops. Caller-local file content crossing to the canonical host must use explicit byte-transfer methods, not server-local path strings. Server-local paths returned in read models are diagnostic hints, not remote filesystem guarantees.
- **enforced_by:** `Locator parsing and shared pkg/client transport selection; wrkq/wrkf initialize validation of protocol version, schema hash, and required method/capability surface before business dispatch; daemon and bootstrap migration-readiness refusal before RPC exposure; nodeauth token-to-node resolution, shared-token supersession, and request-context attachment; the live max3→mini cutover; and the wrkq.verify-gate local handoff control.`

## wrkq.task-claim.authority

- **scope:** cross-node task holdership, takeover fencing, and claimed-task completion
- **predicate:** A task claim is one canonical-home SQLite transaction. The server accepts only a verified per-node bearer identity, derives claimed_node from that identity, validates an exact task-scoped agent ScopeRef whose agent matches the caller principal, and atomically records the full holder tuple while setting the task in_progress. The durable claim_generation starts at zero and can only increase; release clears the tuple but never resets generation. Takeover always mints a new token and increments generation. Completion of a claimed task validates principal, exact scope, authenticated node, generation, and token inside the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction as completion. Superseded holders cannot validate or complete but may append comments. Claims have no lease or TTL.

## wrkq.task-hierarchy.cross-project-parents

- **scope:** task parent graph, task residency, and hierarchy-affecting mutations
- **predicate:** `tasks.project_uuid` is the authoritative task residency/container path. `tasks.parent_task_uuid` is a bounded task-graph edge, not a container-membership edge, and MAY reference a task whose `project_uuid` differs from the child's. Path/container-scoped machine projections (`tree --json`, `tree --ndjson`, `tree --porcelain`, list/find path filters, and their RPC compatibility shapes) remain scoped by residency unless a future record explicitly changes that machine contract: only tasks resident in the selected container set count as selected/resident tree content. In-set subtask nesting happens when both parent and child are resident and visible in that selected set. Human `wrkq tree` MAY augment a resident parent task with visible external-child backlink rows for cross-residency children. Those rows must be marked as external or otherwise visually unmistakable, and they are presentation/backlink rows only: they are not resident containment, do not change the child's `path` or `project_uuid`, and must not affect recursive delete impact, move membership, path-filter membership, hidden-container counts, or `all_tasks_completed` rollups. If external rows cross the RPC boundary, they must be modeled as explicit non-resident presentation data (or a separate human-tree read model), not as ordinary resident task children silently mixed into machine projections. Cross-residency children also appear in their own residency and task detail/read models may expose the parent id/uuid as a backlink. Parent graph integrity is global: parent existence, no self-parenting, max depth 1, and cycle prevention are enforced across project/container boundaries. Hierarchy-affecting mutations must not let a parent edge delete, move, archive, restore, purge, or otherwise mutate a task with a different `project_uuid` unless that task is explicitly selected by the caller's residency-scoped operation. Same-residency descendants preserve existing containment behavior for the operation being performed. Cross-residency children are external backlinks: when their parent task/container/project is tombstoned or hard-deleted, they are detached (`parent_task_uuid = NULL`; `kind` normalized to `task` unless explicitly set by the caller), not deleted. Unconditional schema-level cascade on `tasks.parent_task_uuid` is forbidden under this invariant. The database default failure mode must be detach or reject; any same-residency cascade is an explicit store/API behavior with tests.
- **enforced_by:** `internal/db/migrations/000031_cross_project_parent_edges.sql; internal/store/tasks.go; internal/store/containers.go; internal/wrkqapi/treeview.go; internal/rpccli/tree.go; internal/wrkqd/tree_http.go; internal/store/cross_project_parent_test.go; internal/workrpc/taskmove_test.go`

## wrkq.wrkf-action.lease-recovery

- **scope:** wrkf.action lease authority recovery and explicit revocation
- **predicate:** Coordinator-owned wrkf.action runs may opt into durable leases. A leased active action run carries one current lease token and non-secret owner/expiry/heartbeat audit fields. Lease TTL expiry only makes a claim contestable: no timer, CLI command, RPC method, or service path mutates the run at expiry. Settlement with current token authority remains valid after expiry unless that authority is explicitly revoked. Before holder settlement, revocation has exactly two external paths. First, a successor must acknowledge the latest predecessor by run id; that claim atomically terminalizes the predecessor as superseded, revokes its token, links the successor, and appends a succession ledger event. Second, an explicit instance terminalization, either suspension close/cancel under a matching suspension id or active unsuspended instance cancel, atomically terminalizes every active run, clears each token, and records the terminal cause and run-finished event in the same transaction as the instance transition. Resume preserves active-run authority. These paths reuse priorRun, the matching suspension id, and ordinary revision CAS; they introduce no expiry gate or additional bearer. Only acknowledged succession or explicit atomic instance terminalization, never wall-clock expiry alone, refuses a late settle.

## wrkq.wrkf-hook.remote-execution

- **scope:** remote wrkf hook, check, and effect execution on the canonical node
- **predicate:** Remote wrkf external execution is canonical-node controlled and request-bounded. Each installed workflow template version stores the canonical hook-catalog body and hash that define its hook law. At execution, the hook or effect handler is selected from that stored body only after the daemon's explicitly configured catalog has the same hash; the daemon configuration supplies the executable bundle root, never replacement hook definitions. A remote caller cannot select a catalog, and wrkqd never uses workspace or home-directory autodiscovery. `wrkf.check.run`, `wrkf.hook.run`, and `wrkf.effect.deliver` execute child processes outside the global workrpc dispatch/stdout critical sections and outside SQLite writer transactions. The remote hook timeout ceiling is positive and strictly below the daemon response deadline. An entry whose effective timeout exceeds that ceiling is refused before execution and before check persistence or effect claim. Request cancellation terminates the child and no check result or effect acknowledgement may commit afterward. Local InProcess execution may retain caller-selected catalogs and an unbounded-by-route policy; crossing the HTTP boundary activates this invariant.
- **enforced_by:** `Template-pinned hook catalog identity, DaemonServer explicit catalog loading, remote CLI catalog-override refusal, external-method lock isolation, and the server-owned hook ceiling below the HTTP response timeout.`
- **source:** `docs/wrkf-remote-transport-migration-spec.md`, `internal/workflow/service.go`, `internal/workflow/ledger.go`, `internal/workflow/hook_catalog_pinning_test.go`, `internal/workflow/hook_isolation_test.go`, `internal/workrpc/bootstrap/bootstrap.go`, `internal/workrpc/bootstrap/hook_catalog_test.go`, `internal/workrpc/server.go`, `internal/workrpc/server_contract_test.go`, `internal/workrpc/limits.go`, `internal/workrpc/limits_test.go`, `internal/wrkfcli/transport.go`, `internal/wrkfcli/transport_test.go`
- **required_tests:** `TestHookExecutionRequiresConfiguredCatalogToMatchStoredTemplateLaw`, `TestDaemonServerNeverAutodiscoversHookCatalog`, `TestConfiguredTransportRejectsHookCatalogOverrideForRemote`, `TestExternalExecutionDoesNotSerializeUnrelatedRPC`, `TestRunChecksHookDoesNotHoldWriterTransaction`, `TestRunChecksRefusesOversizedRemoteTimeoutBeforeExecution`, `TestRunChecksCancellationStopsBeforePersistence`, `TestRemoteHookTimeoutLeavesResponseHeadroom`
- **last_verified:** 2026-07-22

## wrkq.wrkf-rpc.attachment-byte-transfer

- **scope:** attachment content crossing the wrkq/wrkf RPC boundary
- **predicate:** Attachment CONTENT crossing the client↔server RPC boundary must cross as explicit protocol data with a declared encoding (base64), size, and checksum — never as a required server-local host path. The CLI owns reading local stdin/files and writing decoded bytes to stdout or `--as <path>`; the server owns storage, authoritative size validation (vs attachments_max_mb), checksum, metadata/event mutation, and cleanup (temp file + atomic rename). RAW bytes are emitted ONLY by production wrkq after RPC-frame decode — the JSON-RPC server stdout stays JSON-RPC-pure. Absence of byte capability (no explicitly-configured attach dir) HARD-GATES with WRKQ_VALIDATION; it never silently falls back to a host path. A server-local/staged path may exist later ONLY as a distinctly-named local capability (e.g. sharedFilesystemPaths), never the correctness path and never the remote contract. Transfers are CHUNKED because the JSON-RPC frame cap (workrpc.DefaultMaxFrameBytes = 8 MiB) is smaller than the default attach limit (attachments_max_mb = 50 MB): getBytes returns up to 1 MiB raw per frame (+ whole-file size/checksum); addBytes stages chunks into a temp file and atomically renames on the final chunk. The existing wrkq.attachment.add (host-path fast path for a co-located real file) is unaffected and remains local-only.
- **enforced_by:** `wrkq.attachment.getBytes/addBytes (chunked base64 + size + checksum) + the byte-transfer parity/transport/stdout-purity tests; daedalus OPTION 1 ruling hrcchat#10132 (T-05103)`
- **source:** `internal/wrkqapi/attachmentbytes.go`, `internal/rpccli/attach.go`, `internal/workrpc/registry.go`
- **required_tests:** `internal/rpccli/parity_test.go`, `internal/rpccli/transport_test.go`, `internal/wrkqapi/catview_fingerprint_test.go`, `internal/workrpc/catview_catalog_test.go`
- **last_verified:** 2026-06-22

## wrkq.wrkf-rpc.bounded-polling-streaming

- **scope:** monitor + watch live-tailing crossing the wrkq/wrkf RPC boundary
- **predicate:** The `wrkq monitor watch|wait`, `wrkq watch` (+ `monitor watch --raw`), and `wrkf watch` live-tailing surfaces cross the client↔server RPC boundary as BOUNDED POLLING read models — there is NO server push / subscribe / long-lived stream in RPC v1 (daedalus ruling #10211). The SERVER owns ONLY stateless, bounded read models: wrkq.monitor.eventsView returns a single bounded ASCENDING event_log page (selector resolution, resource_id hydration from principal/resource refs, comment→task backfill, isEventIncluded / isStateChangeEvent, event-type filtering, and the high-water cursor of the LAST RAW row scanned); wrkq.monitor.stateView returns a SINGLE authoritative --until condition snapshot (met + still-unmet task ids) and NEVER sleeps/times out/stalls/emits terminal lines; wrkq.history.tailView returns a bounded ASCENDING raw event_log page (principal/resource hydration + high-water). Each page is hard-capped server-side (monitorMaxPageLimit) so a hammering client can never pull an unbounded slice in one frame. The CLIENT (production wrkq) owns ALL streaming control flow: the blocking poll loop + interval, the monotonic high-water cursor carried across polls, the timeout/stall clocks, the per-event NDJSON lines, EXACTLY ONE terminal NDJSON record before exit, the exit codes (0=met, 1=timeout/stall, 2=selector/usage, 3=stream), the deprecation warning (watch), and human/NDJSON rendering. eventsView and stateView are TWO independent snapshots, so the terminal decision is intentionally RACE-TOLERANT (a met condition may be observed before the matching event is paged in); tests assert race-tolerantly. The JSON-RPC server stdout stays JSON-RPC-pure — the per-event / terminal NDJSON is emitted ONLY by production wrkq after RPC-frame decode. The raw tail (watch / monitor --raw) uses WrkqWatchEvent (legacy watchEvent shape: INCLUDES resource_id, STRING timestamp, nullable resource_uuid, and no actor fields), DISTINCT from WrkqLogEvent. The `--last N` replay start cursor is resolved SERVER-SIDE from actual row IDENTITY: eventsView with lastN>0 returns the legacy predicate COALESCE(MIN(id),0)-1 over the last N EXISTING event_log rows (by id DESC) as the high-water cursor with an empty page; the client then streams forward from it applying its selectors/filters. This is GAP-INDEPENDENT: event_log.id is monotonic AUTOINCREMENT identity but is NOT assumed gap-free, so the client MUST NOT compute the start cursor as high_water-N arithmetic (which under-replays when the last N rows span an id gap). No implicit event_log.id contiguity invariant exists or may be relied upon (daedalus ruling #10262).
- **enforced_by:** `wrkq.monitor.eventsView/stateView + wrkq.history.tailView (bounded server read models) + the client-owned poll loop in internal/rpccli/monitor.go + watch.go; daedalus ruling hrcchat#10211 (T-05115 / T-05116)`
- **source:** `internal/wrkqapi/monitorview.go`, `internal/rpccli/monitor.go`, `internal/rpccli/watch.go`, `internal/workrpc/registry.go`, `internal/wrkfapi/gaps.go`, `internal/wrkfcli/watch.go`
- **required_tests:** `internal/rpccli/parity_test.go`, `internal/rpccli/transport_test.go`, `internal/wrkqapi/monitorview_test.go`, `internal/wrkqapi/catview_fingerprint_test.go`, `internal/workrpc/catview_catalog_test.go`, `internal/wrkfcli/watch_test.go`
- **last_verified:** 2026-07-21

## wrkq.wrkf-rpc.search-index-server-owned

- **scope:** server-owned search/index derived state (the <db>.search.sqlite sidecar + dense embedder) behind the wrkq RPC boundary
- **predicate:** The derived <db>.search.sqlite search sidecar AND the dense embedder are SERVER-OWNED and live BEHIND the JSON-RPC boundary (wrkq.search.listView / wrkq.index.{status,update,rebuild,vacuum,pause,resume}). The server owns: opening + migrating the sidecar, freshness/status, FTS5/vec/lexical queries, RRF fusion, canonical filtering, and lifecycle mutation. EnsureLlamaReady lives on the SERVER / index-lifecycle host — index update/rebuild kickstart ONLY the SERVER host's configured embedder, NEVER the caller's launchd; if the server cannot ready its embedder, dense degrades/fails per the existing contract and never reaches back to the client. Search label filters are evaluated against canonical tasks.labels, never sidecar labels/prose/tokens. Membership is exact and case-sensitive; every distinct requested label must be present, duplicate requests are idempotent, and canonical filtering occurs before result pagination. The CLI mirror (internal/rpccli) owns ONLY project-root path scoping (paths are pre-scoped before the call) + presentation. It MUST NOT open the sidecar (internal/search, internal/search/indexdb, internal/search/indexer) or call EnsureLlamaReady (internal/search/embed) — this is enforced structurally by the rpccli import guard, which forbids the internal/search import subtree. Field order is part of the contract: WrkqSearchListView reproduces the legacy search.Response struct order, WrkqSearchResult the legacy search.Result struct order, and WrkqIndexStatus the legacy indexdb.Status struct order (NOT alphabetical). The lifecycle methods return legacy map-shaped acks whose JSON keys are map-ALPHABETICAL, with the nested status block in indexdb.Status struct order. The server search-index path defaults from the server DB config (<db>.search.sqlite). When search is disabled the methods report WRKQ_VALIDATION "search is disabled".
- **enforced_by:** `the server-owned search host (internal/wrkqapi/searchindex.go) + the import-guard forbidding the internal/search subtree in the mirror + the search/index acceptance, transport-equivalence, and parity tests; daedalus B-ruling hrcchat#10211 (T-05114)`
- **source:** `internal/wrkqapi/searchindex.go`, `internal/search/search.go`, `internal/workrpc/registry.go`, `internal/workrpc/bootstrap/bootstrap.go`, `internal/wrkfcli/root.go`, `internal/rpccli/search.go`, `internal/rpccli/index.go`, `internal/rpccli/importguard_test.go`, `internal/wrkqapi/label_filter_test.go`, `internal/rpccli/label_filter_test.go`
- **required_tests:** `internal/wrkqapi/searchindex_test.go`, `internal/wrkqapi/catview_fingerprint_test.go`, `internal/workrpc/catview_catalog_test.go`, `internal/rpccli/importguard_test.go`, `internal/rpccli/searchindex_transport_test.go`, `internal/rpccli/parity_test.go`, `internal/wrkqapi/label_filter_test.go`, `internal/rpccli/label_filter_test.go`
- **last_verified:** 2026-07-24
